title: THE FLOCK THAT FILED A FLIGHT PLAN
deck: Four hundred thousand starlings keep drawing the same shape across an airport's approach path, and the airport has signed a cull for Friday. Illuminara has three dusk trials, one abort word that is not hers, and a message she must read before she can answer it.
shape: Six scenes across three days: a tower, a crescent drawn in light, a trial she gets wrong and a bird that corrects her, a bank the flock chooses twice, a plan with its costs written in, a ventilator flight landing in a clear sky, and a flight plan filed by the flock.

scenes.title: Eleven Minutes of Fuel
paragraphs: *Karst Lowfield Airport, control tower · Wednesday, 15:20*

Femi Adeyinka had watched the same sentence form on his radar for forty-one dusks. On the forty-second he stopped calling it a bird-strike hazard and called it the Crescent, and he said the name aloud to a visitor who had arrived on the afternoon bus and who looked at the replay as if he had shown her a face.

Four hundred thousand starlings rose from the freight apron, thickened into a black bar across the approach path, and bent. The bar became an arc four hundred and ten metres long with a notch cut into its north-eastern end. It held for eleven minutes. Then it dissolved, and the next evening it came back exactly the same.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Forty-one evenings, same outline to within a wingspan. A swarm is weather. Weather doesn't repeat.

**Illuminara**  
No. This is a drawing. Has anyone else seen it?

**Femi Adeyinka**  
The radar sees it. Nobody believed the radar.

Marguerite Soll came in without knocking. She was the airport's safety director, fifty-eight, thirty years of runways in her shoulders, and she carried a folder with a cull order in it and the incident report from the night of the second go-around.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Eleven minutes of fuel. A Lifeline ventilator flight went around twice, and the captain wrote that he could not see the runway lights through the birds. The cull team and the laser line go up on Friday at dusk. I have signed it.

**Illuminara**  
What would change your signature?

**Marguerite Soll**  
Nothing that sounds like feeling. I don't need to be understood by birds. I need the glide path clear when a ventilator flight comes in. If you can promise me that tonight, speak. If you cannot, the laser goes up Friday.

Illuminara did not reach for the answer she could have given. She could hold the whole sky above the approach empty for a night, and for a second night after that; she knew exactly what it would weigh. She also knew what it would leave behind: an airport that needed her, and four hundred thousand birds still saying the same thing to a wall.

**Illuminara**  
I can't promise you the sky tonight. I can offer you a test you can stop. Three trials at dusk, away from the live approach, your hand on the abort. If the flock does not answer the same way three times, tell me to go home and I will.

**Marguerite Soll**  
And if I say abort, you stop. Instantly. Not after one more sweep.

**Illuminara**  
Instantly.
Soll looked at the folder, then at the arc frozen on the screen, then at Femi, who had not asked for anything except one night to be proved wrong.

**Marguerite Soll**  
The north approach is closed to arrivals from 16:20 to 17:10. I'll pay for it. The word is mine.

scenes.title: The Crescent
paragraphs: *The freight apron, beside the lighting truck · Wednesday, 16:31*

The apron floodlights stood in four banks along its edge, new white ones, and behind them lay the slab where the reed beds had been until three winters ago. Femi sat in the lighting truck with the panel on his knee. Soll stood a pace behind Illuminara with a radio held against her coat like a hymn book.

At 16:38 the wall began. It came from the south in streams, folded over the slab, and turned toward the approach path the way it had forty-one times before. This time Illuminara did not look at the wall. She looked at its edge, at the single place where the density changed, and she let it come through her feet as pressure: four hundred thousand wingbeats arriving as one slow weather.

**Illuminara**  
It has three parts. The outline says what. The place says where. And the way it opens at the notch is a question, because it opens toward the lights.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
A question about what?

**Illuminara**  
About whether the warm is still there. Your new banks are the only warm thing on the ground it used to land on. It rises to the lights each evening and checks.
She told Femi the pattern: bank A to bank D in sequence, forty seconds, the outline of the arc drawn in light. Not a flash, not a threat. A sentence slowly spoken.
Femi pressed the panel. Light ran along the apron's edge like a finger tracing a coastline.

For a moment nothing happened. Then the black wall in the sky stopped turning. It folded and thinned, and she thought it would break; instead it drew itself back at her, a crescent, the notch in the right place, half a second late. It wobbled at the tip. It corrected the tip.
Illuminara found that she had stopped breathing. The wall had opened like a curtain, and for the first time in three winters, something had replied.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
It said it back. It said it back.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Once.

The second trial moved the sweep sixty metres east. The crescent followed, sixty metres east, with its notch at the same angle. Soll wrote the time on her wrist with a pen, which was a thing Illuminara noticed she did when she did not want to make a sound.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Twice.

scenes.title: Abort
paragraphs: *The pond edge and the apron · Wednesday, 16:52*

The third trial was Illuminara's, and she had built it in the afternoon with the ground crew: twelve amber construction lamps strung along the drainage ponds six hundred metres north of the glide path, where the old reed margin had run. The idea was simple and she was proud of it. The flock needed a door. She would draw one.

**Illuminara**  
Dim banks A and B to half. Light the ponds. It has asked where the warm is. I'll show it somewhere else.
Femi dimmed the banks. The amber lamps lit along the water, small and warm.

The wall did not turn north. It stopped, and everything in it seemed to lean at once. The density rose at the lower edge. The arc thickened and sank, and the whole bar slid toward the closed approach like a held breath coming out.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Abort.
Illuminara did not reach for the sky. She felt her power wait in her like a held hand, and she left it where it was.

**Illuminara**  
Femi, banks back to full. Now. Lamps off.

The apron blazed white again. The wall hung forty metres from the line Soll had closed. For ten seconds, no one in the truck moved. Then the birds drew a crescent, larger than the first, and this time it wrapped around the apron lights as if holding them. From its notch ran one thin thread of birds pointing north, at the dark ponds.
Illuminara read it twice, because the first time she did not like what it said.

**Illuminara**  
I told it the warm was leaving. It heard the third winter again. And it answered the real question, which I hadn't asked: not instead, as well. Keep the warm here. Add the other.

**Marguerite Soll**  
You were wrong.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. And it corrected me before I could do harm, because you stopped me when you did.

Soll lowered the radio. She looked at the thread of birds, thin as a pencil line, and for the first time her face made the expression of a woman doing arithmetic she had not expected to find in the sum.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Three trials. One failed, and the flock told you why. Is that a pass?

**Illuminara**  
It's the only trial in which it told me something I didn't know.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Then one more, and it is a different kind. Femi, you have the two margins on your panel.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
West bank, nearest the apron lights. East bank, a hundred and fifty metres further from the glide path. I can light either. We have been choosing for it all afternoon. Ask.

**Illuminara**  
Ask so that it can refuse. West then east, then east then west. If it picks the same bank in both orders, the order isn't doing the picking.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Ten minutes. The north approach stays closed to 17:20. The word is still mine.

Femi lit the west bank. The thread in the sky frayed, wavered and doubled back on itself like a sentence someone had lost. He cut the lamps and lit the east bank, and the thread thickened and held, pointed at the dark water a hand's breadth wide. Then he lit east first, and it held, and west, and it frayed. Illuminara had bet on west, closer to the warm. She said so aloud before the second pair, and Soll made her say it twice so that she could write it down.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Twice, in both orders. And it chose the far bank, away from my approach. Coincidence?

**Illuminara**  
Possibly. That is why Femi swapped the order. I would have chosen west. I would have been wrong.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Then go on. Tomorrow I want it in writing, with the east bank in it.

scenes.title: Fog Nights
paragraphs: *The operations room · Wednesday, 20:10*
They wrote it at the long table with the ground plan pinned open and a pot of tea nobody drank. Illuminara proposed; Soll cut. Femi drew the timetable in the margins.

The airport owned the drainage ponds. The ponds would be planted in reed over two seasons. On the east bank, which the flock had chosen twice and which Soll had initialled beside the lamp layout, thirty bundles of cut reed and a rank of cut-reed mats would be staked in the shallows by the end of the week. The apron lights would keep their white edge for ninety minutes each dusk, because the warm was part of the sentence. The amber lamps would stay on the ponds all evening, as the second half of it. At 15:50 a controller would sweep the arc, and if the flock drew it back, the day's call was acknowledged and the birds would be asked to come down early, before the evening arrivals.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Early does not mean certain. What does the first winter cost me?

**Illuminara**  
Honestly? Perhaps six in ten birds will use the ponds while the reeds are stubble. The bundles and mats hold about one bird in six of those; the rest sit on bare bank and shallows, rough sleeping, which is worse for them and no worse for you. The other four in ten stay on the apron fence, off the glide path, if the call holds. On fog nights they won't read the lights at all. Those nights are still risky.

**Marguerite Soll**  
I'll staff the fog nights. I'll take the risk off the tower's name. Lifeline Four is inbound tomorrow at 16:58 with a ventilator patient. If the handshake does not work at 15:50, or the radar does not show a clear window at 16:30, the flight goes to runway 09 and a standby crew at Brandt Field holds fuel for a diversion. Independent of birds, independent of you.

**Illuminara**  
Good. I'd have asked for the same.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
And if the flock says no tomorrow?

**Illuminara**  
Then the answer is no, and Marguerite signs Friday's order with every reason to.
Femi laughed once, in surprise, and then did not. Soll folded the cull order and slid it into the folder without tearing it.

scenes.title: Lifeline Four
paragraphs: *The freight apron · Thursday, 15:50*

The handshake worked at 15:51. Femi's sweep ran the length of the apron, the arc came back in the sky, and then something Illuminara had not designed: the crescent broke at its notch and poured, like a river finding a second bed, north toward the amber lamps on the east bank.
Not all of it. Close to half the flock stayed at the apron's far end, tight and black along the fence. Illuminara counted what she could not count and let Femi's radar do the rest.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Clear window at 16:30. Approach is clear. Twenty-eight minutes to the flight.

Soll stood with her hands in her pockets. She did not look at Illuminara. She looked at the sky above the approach, where the last light was going, and at the dark thread over the ponds, and at the thin bar of birds on the fence that was, she understood now, a part of the answer and not a leftover.

**Lifeline Four**  
Karst, Lifeline Four. Eleven miles. We have the field.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Lifeline Four, Karst, runway two-seven, clear approach, wind calm.
The aircraft came out of the dusk with its landing light pale in the pale air. The birds on the fence did not move.

**Lifeline Four**  
Short final. Sky is clear. Whoever moved the starlings, tell them thanks.
It touched. The ambulance was already moving.
Soll stood a long time after the tail lights had gone. Then she took the folded order from her coat and held it out to Femi, as if she did not trust her own hand to put it away.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Suspended. Not cancelled. The laser line stays in the cabinet with my name on the key. At the first fog night I decide again.

**Illuminara**  
That is the right amount.

**Marguerite Soll**  
I haven't changed my mind about birds. I've changed my mind about asking them. If they take the ponds, tell them I'll stand by the reeds.

**Illuminara**  
You can tell them yourself. At 15:50. Femi will show you the panel.

scenes.title: The Plan
paragraphs: *The control tower · Friday, 15:48*

A night controller had put in for transfer to Brandt before the end of the week. She would not work the bird protocol, she said, and Soll signed the transfer without argument, because the refusal was hers to make.

Femi sat at the movement board with the panel beside him. At 15:50 he swept the arc. The flock drew it back, and from the notch came the thread north, thicker than the day before, a hand's breadth now rather than a pencil line.

He entered it on the board where he entered departures, in his plain block capitals: STARLING FLOCK, ROOST, PONDS NORTH, EAST BANK, 16:20 TO 16:50, ACKNOWLEDGED. EST SIX IN TEN. Under it he wrote the weather forecast for Saturday. Fog.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
They filed a flight plan.

**Marguerite Soll**  
They'll need a fog plan too.

Illuminara had gone out onto the east bank in the last light with the ground crew. Thirty bundles of cut reed and a rank of mats stood in the shallows, knee-high, absurd and small, room for one bird in six. The amber lamps came on one after another along the margin.

Above her, the wall opened like a curtain over the ponds. The flock came down in slow, long streams, some into the bundles and the mats, more onto the bare bank and the shallows beside them, crowded and rough, while four in ten held the apron fence behind the white lights, off the glide path, the part of the sentence that was theirs.

critic_line: Illuminara learns that the flock's crescent is a correction rather than consent, so Femi's observations, Soll's abort authority and the birds' repeated east-bank choice jointly create a safe flight window and an honestly partial new home without turning understanding into control.

translation_sl.title: JATA, KI JE VLOŽILA NAČRT LETA
translation_sl.deck: Štiristo tisoč škorcev nad priletno potjo letališča vztrajno riše isto obliko, letališče pa je za petek podpisalo odstrel. Illuminara ima tri preizkuse v mraku, eno besedo za prekinitev, ki ni njena, in sporočilo, ki ga mora prebrati, preden lahko nanj odgovori.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v treh dneh: stolp, polmesec, narisan s svetlobo, preizkus, pri katerem se zmoti, in ptica, ki jo popravi, breg, ki ga jata izbere dvakrat, načrt z zapisanimi stroški, let z ventilatorjem, ki pristane pod jasnim nebom, in načrt leta, ki ga vloži jata.

scenes.title: Enajst minut goriva
paragraphs: *Letališče Karst Lowfield, kontrolni stolp · sreda, 15:20*

Femi Adeyinka je enainštirideset mrakov opazoval, kako se na njegovem radarju oblikuje isti stavek. Dvainštiridesetič ga je nehal imenovati nevarnost trka s pticami in ga poimenoval Polmesec; ime je izrekel na glas obiskovalki, ki je prispela s popoldanskim avtobusom in posnetek gledala, kakor da ji je pokazal obraz.

Štiristo tisoč škorcev se je dvignilo s tovorne ploščadi, se zgostilo v črno prečko čez priletno pot in zavilo. Prečka je postala štiristo deset metrov dolg lok z zarezo na severovzhodnem koncu. Vztrajal je enajst minut. Nato se je razblinil, naslednji večer pa se je vrnil popolnoma enak.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Enainštirideset večerov, isti obris do razpona enega krila. Roj je vreme. Vreme se ne ponavlja.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. To je risba. Jo je videl še kdo?

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Radar jo vidi. Radarju ni verjel nihče.

Marguerite Soll je vstopila brez trkanja. Bila je oseminpetdesetletna direktorica letališke varnosti, s tridesetimi leti vzletno-pristajalnih stez v ramenih, in nosila je mapo z odredbo za odstrel ter poročilo o dogodku iz noči drugega prekinjenega pristanka.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Enajst minut goriva. Let Lifeline z ventilatorjem je moral dvakrat prekiniti pristanek, kapitan pa je zapisal, da skozi ptice ni videl steznih luči. Ekipa za odstrel in laserska linija se v petek ob mraku aktivirata. Podpisala sem.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi spremenilo vaš podpis?

**Marguerite Soll**  
Nič, kar zveni kakor čustvo. Ne potrebujem, da me ptice razumejo. Potrebujem prosto drsno pot, ko prihaja let z ventilatorjem. Če mi lahko to obljubite za nocoj, govorite. Če ne, se laser v petek aktivira.

Illuminara ni posegla po odgovoru, ki bi ga lahko dala. Za eno noč bi lahko ohranila prazno vse nebo nad priletno potjo in nato še drugo; natanko je vedela, koliko bi jo to stalo. Vedela pa je tudi, kaj bi ostalo: letališče, ki bi jo potrebovalo, in štiristo tisoč ptic, ki bi zidu še vedno govorile isto.

**Illuminara**  
Za nocoj vam ne morem obljubiti neba. Lahko vam ponudim preizkus, ki ga lahko ustavite. Tri preizkušnje ob mraku, stran od aktivne priletne poti, vi pa imate v rokah prekinitev. Če jata trikrat ne odgovori enako, mi recite, naj grem domov, in bom šla.

**Marguerite Soll**  
In če rečem prekinitev, se ustavite. Takoj. Ne po še enem zamahu.

**Illuminara**  
Takoj.
Soll je pogledala mapo, nato na zaslonu zamrznjeni lok in zatem Femija, ki ni prosil za nič drugega kot eno noč, v kateri bi se lahko izkazalo, da se moti.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Severna priletna pot bo za prihode zaprta od 16:20 do 17:10. Plačala jo bom. Beseda je moja.

scenes.title: Polmesec
paragraphs: *Tovorna ploščad ob tovornjaku za razsvetljavo · sreda, 16:31*

Ob robu ploščadi so stale štiri skupine reflektorjev, novi beli, za njimi pa je ležala betonska površina, kjer je bilo še pred tremi zimami trstičje. Femi je sedel v tovornjaku za razsvetljavo s krmilno ploščo na kolenu. Soll je stala korak za Illuminaro in radijsko postajo držala ob plašču kakor pesmarico.

Ob 16:38 se je začel oblikovati zid. Z juga je prihajal v tokovih, se prepognil čez ploščad in obrnil proti priletni poti, kakor je to storil že enainštiridesetkrat. Tokrat Illuminara ni gledala zidu. Gledala je njegov rob, edino mesto, kjer se je gostota spremenila, in pustila, da je skozi stopala prišel do nje kakor pritisk: štiristo tisoč zamahov kril, ki so prihajali kakor eno počasno vreme.

**Illuminara**  
Ima tri dele. Obris pove kaj. Kraj pove kje. Način, kako se odpre pri zarezi, pa je vprašanje, ker se odpira proti lučem.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Vprašanje o čem?

**Illuminara**  
O tem, ali je toplota še tam. Vaše nove skupine luči so edina topla stvar na tleh, na katerih je nekoč pristajala. Vsak večer se dvigne k lučem in preveri.
Femiju je opisala vzorec: skupine od A do D zapored, štirideset sekund, obris loka, narisan s svetlobo. Ne blisk, ne grožnja. Počasi izgovorjen stavek.
Femi je pritisnil krmilnik. Svetloba je tekla ob robu ploščadi kakor prst, ki sledi obali.

Za trenutek se ni zgodilo nič. Nato se je črni zid na nebu nehal obračati. Prepognil se je in stanjšal in mislila je, da bo razpadel; namesto tega se je narisal nazaj proti njej, polmesec z zarezo na pravem mestu, pol sekunde prepozno. Konica je zanihala. Popravil je konico.
Illuminara je ugotovila, da je nehala dihati. Zid se je odprl kakor zavesa in prvič v treh zimah je nekaj odgovorilo.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Ponovila ga je. Ponovila ga je.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Enkrat.

Pri drugem preizkusu so zamah premaknili šestdeset metrov proti vzhodu. Polmesec mu je sledil šestdeset metrov proti vzhodu, z zarezo pod enakim kotom. Soll si je čas s pisalom zapisala na zapestje; Illuminara je opazila, da to počne, kadar noče izpustiti glasu.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Dvakrat.

scenes.title: Prekinitev
paragraphs: *Rob ribnika in ploščad · sreda, 16:52*

Tretji preizkus je bil Illuminarin in popoldne ga je zgradila z zemeljsko ekipo: dvanajst jantarnih gradbiščnih svetilk, razvrščenih ob zadrževalnih ribnikih šeststo metrov severno od drsne poti, kjer je nekoč potekal rob trstičja. Zamisel je bila preprosta in bila je ponosna nanjo. Jata je potrebovala vrata. Ona jih bo narisala.

**Illuminara**  
Zatemni skupini A in B na polovico. Osvetli ribnike. Vprašala je, kje je toplota. Pokazala ji jo bom drugje.
Femi je zatemnil skupini. Ob vodi so se prižgale majhne, tople jantarne svetilke.

Zid ni zavil proti severu. Ustavil se je in zdelo se je, da se vse v njem hkrati nagiba. Gostota ob spodnjem robu je narasla. Lok se je odebelil in spustil, vsa prečka pa je zdrsnila proti zaprti priletni poti kakor zadržan dih, ki uhaja.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Prekinitev.
Illuminara ni posegla po nebu. Čutila je svojo moč, ki je v njej čakala kakor zadržana roka, in pustila jo je tam.

**Illuminara**  
Femi, skupine spet na polno. Zdaj. Svetilke ugasni.

Ploščad je znova zažarela belo. Zid je obstal štirideset metrov od črte, ki jo je zaprla Soll. Deset sekund se v tovornjaku ni premaknil nihče. Nato so ptice narisale polmesec, večji od prvega, in tokrat je objel luči na ploščadi, kakor da jih drži. Iz njegove zareze je tekla ena tanka nit ptic in kazala proti severu, k temnim ribnikom.
Illuminara ga je prebrala dvakrat, ker ji prvič ni bilo všeč, kar je povedal.

**Illuminara**  
Povedala sem ji, da toplota odhaja. Slišala je tretjo zimo znova. Odgovorila pa je na pravo vprašanje, ki ga nisem zastavila: ne namesto, temveč tudi. Ohranite toploto tukaj. Dodajte drugo.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Motili ste se.

**Illuminara**  
Da. In popravila me je, preden bi lahko povzročila škodo, ker ste me ustavili, ko ste me.
Soll je spustila radijsko postajo. Pogledala je nit ptic, tanko kakor poteza s svinčnikom, in prvič se je na njenem obrazu pojavil izraz ženske, ki računa nekaj, česar v seštevku ni pričakovala.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Trije preizkusi. Eden je spodletel in jata vam je povedala zakaj. Je to uspeh?

**Illuminara**  
To je edini preizkus, pri katerem mi je povedala nekaj, česar nisem vedela.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Potem še eden, vendar drugačen. Femi, na plošči imate oba bregova.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Zahodni breg, najbližji lučem na ploščadi. Vzhodni breg, sto petdeset metrov dlje od drsne poti. Osvetlim lahko katerega koli. Vse popoldne smo izbirali namesto jate. Vprašajte.

**Illuminara**  
Vprašajte tako, da bo lahko zavrnila. Najprej zahod, nato vzhod; potem vzhod, nato zahod. Če obakrat izbere isti breg, izbire ni določil vrstni red.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Deset minut. Severna priletna pot ostane zaprta do 17:20. Beseda je še vedno moja.

Femi je osvetlil zahodni breg. Nit na nebu se je razcefrala, zanihala in se zavila nazaj vase kakor stavek, ki ga je nekdo izgubil. Ugasnil je svetilke in osvetlil vzhodni breg; nit se je zgostila in obstala ter kazala k temni vodi, široka za dlan. Nato je najprej osvetlil vzhod in držala je, potem zahod in razcefrala se je. Illuminara je stavila na zahod, bližje toploti. To je povedala na glas pred drugim parom, Soll pa jo je prisilila, da je ponovila dvakrat, da si je lahko zapisala.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Dvakrat, v obeh vrstnih redih. In izbrala je oddaljeni breg, stran od moje priletne poti. Naključje?

**Illuminara**  
Morda. Zato je Femi zamenjal vrstni red. Jaz bi izbrala zahod. Motila bi se.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Potem nadaljujte. Jutri želim načrt v pisni obliki, z vzhodnim bregom v njem.

scenes.title: Meglene noči
paragraphs: *Operativna soba · sreda, 20:10*
Napisali so ga za dolgo mizo z razgrnjenim tlorisom in loncem čaja, ki ga ni pil nihče. Illuminara je predlagala; Soll je rezala. Femi je v robove risal časovnico.

Letališče je bilo lastnik zadrževalnih ribnikov. V dveh sezonah bi jih zasadili s trstičjem. Na vzhodnem bregu, ki ga je jata izbrala dvakrat in ob katerem je Soll na načrtu svetilk dodala začetnici, bi do konca tedna v plitvino pritrdili trideset snopov porezanega trstičja in vrsto preprog iz trstičja. Luči na ploščadi bi vsak mrak devetdeset minut ohranile bel rob, ker je bila toplota del stavka. Jantarne svetilke ob ribnikih bi gorele ves večer kot njegov drugi del. Ob 15:50 bi kontrolor zarisal lok; če bi ga jata narisala nazaj, bi bil dnevni klic potrjen, ptice pa bi povabili, naj se spustijo zgodaj, pred večernimi prihodi.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Zgodaj ne pomeni zagotovo. Koliko me bo stala prva zima?

**Illuminara**  
Pošteno? Morda bo šest od desetih ptic uporabljalo ribnike, dokler je trstičje le strnišče. Snopi in preproge sprejmejo približno eno od šestih izmed njih; preostale sedijo na golem bregu in v plitvini, spijo neudobno, kar je slabše zanje in nič slabše za vas. Druge štiri od desetih ostanejo na ograji ploščadi, zunaj drsne poti, če klic drži. V meglenih nočeh luči sploh ne bodo prebrale. Tiste noči ostajajo tvegane.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Meglene noči bom kadrovsko pokrila. Tveganje bom prevzela z imena stolpa. Lifeline Four prihaja jutri ob 16:58 s pacientom na ventilatorju. Če rokovanje ob 15:50 ne uspe ali radar ob 16:30 ne pokaže prostega okna, let pristane na stezi 09, rezervna posadka na letališču Brandt Field pa ohrani gorivo za preusmeritev. Neodvisno od ptic, neodvisno od vas.

**Illuminara**  
Dobro. Sama bi zahtevala enako.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
In če jata jutri reče ne?

**Illuminara**  
Potem je odgovor ne in Marguerite petkovo odredbo podpiše z vsemi razlogi.
Femi se je enkrat zasmejal od presenečenja, nato pa ne več. Soll je prepognila odredbo za odstrel in jo, ne da bi jo raztrgala, potisnila v mapo.

scenes.title: Lifeline Four
paragraphs: *Tovorna ploščad · četrtek, 15:50*

Rokovanje je uspelo ob 15:51. Femijev zamah je stekel vzdolž ploščadi, lok se je vrnil na nebu, nato pa se je zgodilo nekaj, česar Illuminara ni načrtovala: polmesec se je pri zarezi prelomil in se kakor reka, ki najde drugo strugo, izlil proti severu, k jantarnih svetilkam na vzhodnem bregu.
Ne ves. Skoraj polovica jate je ostala na oddaljenem koncu ploščadi, gosta in črna ob ograji. Illuminara je štela, česar ni mogla prešteti, in ostalo prepustila Femijevemu radarju.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Prosto okno ob 16:30. Priletna pot je prosta. Osemindvajset minut do leta.

Soll je stala z rokami v žepih. Ni gledala Illuminare. Gledala je nebo nad priletno potjo, kjer je ugašala zadnja svetloba, in temno nit nad ribniki ter tanko prečko ptic na ograji, ki je bila, kakor je zdaj razumela, del odgovora in ne ostanek.

**Lifeline Four**  
Karst, Lifeline Four. Enajst milj. Letališče vidimo.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Lifeline Four, Karst, steza dve-sedem, priletna pot prosta, veter miren.
Letalo se je pojavilo iz mraka s pristajalno lučjo, bledo v bledem zraku. Ptice na ograji se niso premaknile.

**Lifeline Four**  
Kratki finale. Nebo je prosto. Kdor koli je premaknil škorce, mu povejte hvala.
Dotaknilo se je tal. Reševalno vozilo se je že premikalo.
Soll je še dolgo stala, potem ko so zadnje luči izginile. Nato je iz plašča vzela prepognjeno odredbo in jo ponudila Femiju, kakor da ne zaupa lastni roki, da jo pospravi.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Začasno ustavljena. Ne preklicana. Laserska linija ostane v omari, ključ pa je pri meni. Ob prvi megleni noči odločam znova.

**Illuminara**  
To je prava mera.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Glede ptic si nisem premislila. Premislila sem si glede tega, ali jih vprašati. Če sprejmejo ribnike, jim povejte, da bom stala ob trstičju.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko jim poveste sami. Ob 15:50. Femi vam bo pokazal ploščo.

scenes.title: Načrt
paragraphs: *Kontrolni stolp · petek, 15:48*

Nočna kontrolorka je pred koncem tedna zaprosila za premestitev na Brandt. Povedala je, da ne bo izvajala protokola za ptice, Soll pa je premestitev brez ugovora podpisala, ker je bila zavrnitev njena pravica.

Femi je sedel ob tabli gibanj, krmilna plošča pa je bila poleg njega. Ob 15:50 je zarisal lok. Jata ga je narisala nazaj in iz zareze je proti severu prišla nit, debelejša kot dan prej, zdaj široka za dlan in ne več kakor poteza s svinčnikom.

Vpisal jo je na tablo, kamor je vpisoval odhode, s svojimi preprostimi tiskanimi črkami: JATA ŠKORCEV, PRENOČIŠČE, RIBNIKI SEVER, VZHODNI BREG, OD 16:20 DO 16:50, POTRJENO. OCENA ŠEST OD DESETIH. Pod to je zapisal vremensko napoved za soboto. Megla.

**Femi Adeyinka**  
Vložili so načrt leta.

**Marguerite Soll**  
Potrebovali bodo tudi načrt za meglo.

Illuminara je z zemeljsko ekipo odšla na vzhodni breg v zadnji svetlobi. Trideset snopov porezanega trstičja in vrsta preprog so stali v plitvini, visoki do kolen, absurdni in majhni, s prostorom za eno ptico od šestih. Jantarne svetilke so se ob robu prižigale druga za drugo.

Nad njo se je zid odprl kakor zavesa nad ribniki. Jata se je spuščala v počasnih dolgih tokovih, nekaj ptic v snope in preproge, več na goli breg in v plitvino ob njih, stisnjeno in neudobno, medtem ko so štiri od desetih ostale na ograji ploščadi za belimi lučmi, zunaj drsne poti, del stavka, ki je bil njihov.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara spozna, da je polmesec jate popravek in ne privolitev, zato Femijeva opazovanja, Sollina pristojnost za prekinitev in ponovljena izbira vzhodnega brega skupaj ustvarijo varno časovno okno za let ter pošteno delen novi dom, ne da bi razumevanje spremenili v nadzor.
